goal: Make a change to quality's or finances' briefs/TEMPLATE.md (which shapes every weekly brief) need a change record, while the dated brief files beside it stay exempt.
changed: A .changes/exempt entry can be a git glob (briefs/[0-9]*.md): * stays within one folder, ** crosses folders. Plain paths match as before. An entry whose first folder is a pattern is refused, so no entry can exempt the whole repo. debrief 0.4.0, bstack 0.40.0.

The template keeps its path: it is a convention shared by quality's AGENTS.md and weekly prompt (also pasted into a scheduled task outside the repo), and agent-kit's qualitydirector and cfo-brief skills.

claims.claim: A glob entry exempts the dated briefs but not TEMPLATE.md beside them, * does not cross folders, plain entries behave as before, and an entry starting with a pattern is refused.
claims.check: tests/test_debrief.py, 43 tests on throwaway git repos; two mutations (literal matching, no first-folder guard) each fail tests
claims.remaining: Which files a glob covers is git's pathspec glob, not Python's; only the cases in the tests are pinned down.

claims.claim: With quality and finances exempting briefs/[0-9]*.md instead of briefs/, every PR since 2026-11-21 in the three repos gets the same verdict as before.
claims.check: replay.sh over 44 PRs with this commit's debrief.py and no --observe; verdicts written before the run all matched, and a run with empty lists failed the brief PRs
claims.remaining: No PR in the window changed TEMPLATE.md without a record, so the new failure shows only in the tests and in the quality and finances PRs' own checks.

next.item: Pin this commit in quality and finances and exempt briefs/[0-9]*.md instead of briefs/
next.source: inferred, from the H16 follow-up on briefs/TEMPLATE.md
next.why_now: Until then a template change in either repo merges with no record
next.impact: A change to what the weekly brief says has to state what it proved
